cards.title: Audit H1-H6 heading hierarchy on a product or category page
cards.summary: Use browser search to verify one H1 per page and check that H2/H3 subheadings structure product and category copy for readability and rankings.
cards.use_when: Auditing a PDP, collection page or landing page for on-page SEO before or after a content refresh.
steps: Open the live page, right-click and choose Inspect, then press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on Mac) and type 'h1' to see whether exactly one H1 exists — the source says a page should have only one H1.
Confirm the H1 is the page's main heading, is clear to a visitor and is at least four characters long; use it for the primary page topic (e.g. the product name or category term).
Search 'h2' in the same way to check that subheadings break up body copy: the source treats H2 as the second-level heading used to make content easier to read.
Treat H3–H6 as bullet/sub-point levels under the H2s.
For blog or guide content (which supports PDPs), verify the article title sits in the H1 and each paragraph section heading sits in an H2.
If a page has zero or multiple H1s, ask your developer to correct the template rather than patching each page, since heading tags are generated by the page template.
caveats: This is the source's stated rule for H1 uniqueness and length; search engines may still parse pages that violate it, but the source frames it as an on-page best practice.
Some tools show metadata and heading structure differently from raw HTML — verify in source code (Ctrl+U) when a plugin's report disagrees.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Write concise, descriptive titles for product and collection pages
cards.summary: Use accurate page titles rather than a fixed 160-character rule.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting title tags for product, category or blog pages before an SEO or paid-search push.
steps: Write a unique, descriptive title reflecting the page's actual product or collection.
Include the primary query naturally without stuffing variants.
Preview likely display and place important words early; Google may truncate or rewrite the displayed title.
caveats: Google sets no fixed title-element character limit; display depends on available width.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Build and submit an XML sitemap to help Google discover sellable URLs
cards.summary: Create an XML sitemap listing your pages, confirm it exposes product/category/blog URLs, and submit it so search engines can crawl and index them.
cards.use_when: Launching a new store, adding a large batch of SKUs or categories, or diagnosing why pages aren't indexed.
steps: Check whether a sitemap exists by appending /sitemap.xml to the homepage; the source says ~99% of sites open this way.
Confirm the sitemap exposes the URL types you want indexed — the source's example shows separate URL groups for products, sitemap pages and blog content.
Prefer the XML sitemap for search engines: the source contrasts XML (understood by search engines, used for crawling/indexing) with HTML sitemaps (aimed at human visitors, not the priority).
If URLs are missing, have your developer generate an updated sitemap (CMS or plugin), then submit it in Google Search Console and monitor indexing.
Re-run this check after large catalog changes, since new product URLs won't be submitted automatically.
caveats: The source presents sitemap XML as the important variant for indexing; an HTML sitemap still helps users but is not the crawl-submission mechanism.
Sitemaps inform Google rather than force indexing — pages still have to be crawlable and non-duplicate.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use canonical tags to prevent duplicate product and category pages from competing
cards.summary: Inspect canonical tags to confirm each product/category URL self-references, signalling uniqueness and blocking duplicate-content dilution.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing cannibalized rankings after variant URLs, filters, or syndicated product copy create near-duplicates.
steps: Open the page, view source (Ctrl+U), press Ctrl+F and search 'canon' to locate the canonical tag.
Verify the canonical URL matches that page's own URL — the source says the same URL should appear, meaning the content is specific to this domain and not pointing at another page.
Repeat on an internal product page (e.g. a power cords page) to confirm it also self-canonicalizes rather than pointing to the homepage or another SKU.

If a page points elsewhere, ask your developer why; syndicated brand copy or manufacturer descriptions are a common cause of duplicated content, and self-canonicalizing asserts the page as the original in the source's framing.
Re-check after any replatform or filter/navigation change, because canonical output is template-driven.
caveats: The source explains canonicalization conceptually; it does not benchmark ranking lifts, and search engines may override canonicals.
The source notes that if someone copies your page, Google will consider the canonical-owning page first — this is the source's framing, not a guarantee against scrapers.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Speed up load times by compressing images and video
cards.summary: Diagnose FCP/LCP in PageSpeed Insights and Search Console, then compress media to hit the source's one-to-two-second load target and reduce bounce.
cards.use_when: Improving storefront load speed when media-heavy PDPs or category pages bounce visitors or score low on mobile.
steps: Run the page through Google PageSpeed Insights and check FCP (first contentful paint — when the first element paints after landing) and LCP (largest contentful paint — when the page's primary content loads).
In Google Search Console, identify which pages have low page-speed scores on mobile and desktop so you prioritize the worst offenders.
Reduce page size by optimizing and compressing images and videos; the source repeatedly flags large media as the first thing to trim.
Target a load time of under one to two seconds, which the source frames as the threshold for a good experience; slower loads drive bounce.
Have a developer implement compression in code rather than relying solely on a plugin, because plugins/extensions can expire or need upgrades.
caveats: The one-to-two-second target is the source's stated guideline, not a measured benchmark for every store.
The source notes that aggressively modifying images may reduce their appeal to visitors, so balance compression against visual quality.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Optimize URLs for clarity and crawlability
cards.summary: Make URLs readable and keyword-relevant, and keep stray numbers, question marks and equals signs out of customer-facing page addresses.
cards.use_when: Setting up new product or category URL structures, or cleaning up messy legacy URLs before SEO work.
steps: Give each page a descriptive, keyword-relevant slug so users and Google can tell the page is about a specific topic (the source's example: skincare products, not a generic parameter string).
Remove numbers, question marks, equals signs and similar parameter noise from URLs that are meant to rank.
Ensure URL statuses are correct (no broken paths) and easy to share, since the source lists easy sharing, performance and research as URL-optimization benefits.
Apply the same discipline to app-store listings and video content if those are part of your acquisition mix — the source extends keyword-optimization thinking to apps and YouTube.
Check old URLs after any change and redirect them, because the source calls out 404 (not-found) pages and dead links as errors to resolve via redirects to relevant pages.
caveats: Changing live URLs requires redirects; the source does not detail redirect mapping, so plan that with your developer.
The source's claims are directional (readability and keyword relevance aid ranking) rather than measured lifts.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Make the mobile experience the primary storefront design
cards.summary: Design and audit the store for phones first — responsive layout, visible options and touch-friendly interaction — since most purchasing happens on mobile.
cards.use_when: Reviewing store design or a PDP/checkout experience where mobile bounce or drop-off is high.
steps: Treat mobile as the default: the source states 70-80% of sales come from mobile and that shoppers use marketplace and shopping apps heavily.
Design so all key options are visible on a small screen, accounting for small screens, limited bandwidth and touch-based interaction rather than hover.
Use responsive design so one site serves desktop, tablet and phone screen sizes effectively; the source rates it as more efficient than adaptive designs.
Build or maintain a mobile app where it helps you target specific customers, and promote it through social channels with relevant news and hashtags.

Perform app store optimization too: proper app titles and icons, a catchy and to-the-point description, relevant keywords, and attention to reviews and positive ratings, which the source says drive app-store visibility.
Check content and UX on mobile after every site change, since the source ties mobile usability to time-on-page and purchase actions.
caveats: The 70-80% mobile-sales figure is the presenter's stated estimate, not a universal benchmark — check your own analytics.
Responsive design is the source's preferred approach; adaptive designs are acknowledged as an alternative, not invalid.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Design an SEO-friendly site architecture with navigation and interlinking
cards.summary: Structure categories and internal links so visitors navigate confidently and crawlers spread authority evenly and reach every page.
cards.use_when: Planning or fixing store information architecture, category hierarchy, or internal linking before scaling a catalog.
steps: Build a clear hierarchy of categories and subcategories so shoppers can find products by intent (the source's example: power cords, bulk wire, extension cords with their own sub-menus).
Use a clickable logo, predictable navigation, click-worthy links, column-based layout and a goal-oriented, consistent layout across pages.

Interlink related pages — the source notes you will mostly find this in blog content, where a mention of 'computer power cord' links to that product page, passing context and visitors to the money page.
Consider segmenting navigation by use case or customer type (the source gives age-band menus) to encourage deeper browsing and even out internal page authority.
Fix crawl obstacles so the bot can traverse the hierarchy; the source warns indexing slows when a site is complex to crawl.
Review the architecture from the shopper's perspective: the source argues good architecture builds customer relationships, confidence in products and conversions — not just rankings.
caveats: The source describes architecture benefits qualitatively; it notes authority spreads evenly only when a site is well designed, and content differences can still cause uneven distribution.
Avoid keyword stuffing while adding internal links — the source explicitly warns against it.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use Yoast (or an equivalent SEO plugin) for WordPress store page metadata and sitemaps
cards.summary: Manage WordPress page titles, descriptions, schemas, sitemaps and 404 handling through an SEO plugin, treating it as configuration rather than magic.
cards.use_when: Maintaining on-page SEO on a WordPress or WooCommerce store without hand-editing templates.
steps: Confirm the plugin (the source uses Yoast as the example) surfaces per-page SEO metadata and meta-description suggestions for titles and descriptions.
Use it to format titles and descriptions and to implement schema for the relevant page type.
Let it generate and manage the XML sitemap and keep advanced sitemap functions current.
Monitor for 404 (not-found) pages and dead links and set redirects to relevant replacement pages.
Treat plugins as replaceable infrastructure: the source warns that plugins/extensions can expire or need upgrading, so have a developer able to do manual fixes.
Verify the current plugin interface before following any step-by-step, since WordPress admin UIs change between versions.
caveats: The source's plugin guidance is WordPress-specific; other CMSs need equivalent tooling.
The presenter advises against depending solely on plugins for tasks like image optimization, preferring developer-implemented code.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Implement schema markup to win rich results for products and reviews
cards.summary: Generate schema JSON-LD with a tool, validate it, and have it installed so Google can surface star ratings, prices and offers in results.
cards.use_when: PDP or category SEO work where you want review stars, price and availability displayed in search results to lift click-through.
steps: Pick the schema type matching the page: product (with offer/review/aggregate rating) for PDPs; article/blog posting for content pages; local business for store location pages.

Generate the code with a schema generator (the source demoed technicalseo.com) rather than writing JSON-LD by hand — fill in name, image URL, brand, description, SKU/identification, offer URL, currency and price.
Note which types the source says still work in its demo (product, offer, aggregate offer, aggregate rating, local/restaurant) and that many older types were deprecated by Google.
Validate the generated code in a rich-results/snippet checker; the source's demo showed a non-critical 'invalid date and time' warning that was fixed by asking an AI assistant to correct the code.
Pass the validated code to your developer to install in the page head, or inject it via Google Tag Manager if backend editing isn't possible.
Re-validate after install and after template changes, since mismatched product data can break rich-result eligibility.
caveats: The source's list of working/banned schema types is drawn from its own demo and may not reflect Google's current supported list — verify against current documentation.
Schema helps eligibility for rich results; it does not itself raise rankings, and only correctly matching data should be marked up.
Use an AI assistant for code fixes only as the source demonstrated — validate output rather than trusting it.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Set up robots.txt to guide crawlers away from cart, checkout and admin URLs
cards.summary: Use robots.txt to disallow crawler access to irrelevant or private paths and direct crawl attention to product, category and content pages.
cards.use_when: Technical SEO audit on a store where crawl budget is being spent on admin, cart or checkout URLs instead of sellable pages.
steps: Check an existing file by appending /robots.txt to the domain; the source's example shows disallowed paths such as admin, checkout and cart URLs.
Decide deliberately what to block: the source blocks admin/back-end and transactional paths and keeps product pages, distribution, blogs and key content open to crawlers.
Write the file in the syntax matching your platform — the source shows that Magento and WordPress (via Yoast) each have their own guidance and parameters, so look up your CMS's current format.
Have a developer apply the file rather than editing server files yourself if you're not comfortable in the back end.
Re-check the file after large site changes, and verify blocked paths aren't accidentally hiding product or category URLs.
caveats: The source stresses robots.txt shouldn't block pages you need indexed; blocking cart/checkout type URLs is presented as standard hygiene, not a universal rule for every path.
robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing — a blocked URL can still appear if linked elsewhere, so pair with noindex where appropriate.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Understand crawl, index and rank mechanics to diagnose ranking problems
cards.summary: Explain how crawlers seed from indexed URLs, follow links and store content — and use that to reason about why pages aren't ranking.
cards.use_when: Investigating why new pages or products aren't appearing in search despite good content, or comparing your crawl coverage to a competitor's.
steps: Treat a new site realistically: the source says a brand-new store can't rank on page one immediately because already-indexed, authoritative pages dominate results first.
Think of crawling as seeded from already-known URLs that expand via hyperlinks — which is why strong interlinking speeds up discovery of new products.
Use Search Console coverage reports to compare pages crawled versus pages published; the source's example questions why only 150 of 200 pages were crawled.
Spot-check the uncrawled pages against competitor equivalents to see what they have (links, content type, structure) that you lack.
Recognize how crawlers use robots.txt to decide what to crawl, and that pages must be crawled and indexed before they can rank.
Re-crawl and re-check after fixes rather than assuming a single change will surface immediately.
caveats: The source describes crawl mechanics conceptually and does not give a timeline for indexing new pages.
Indexing also depends on other factors (duplication, canonicalization, content) beyond crawl access.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Choose keyword research tools by job: domain/catalog audit vs. traffic analysis
cards.summary: Use a domain-level tool to audit what your site already ranks for and where backlinks exist, and a flow tool to examine traffic and keyword movement.
cards.use_when: Starting SEO work on an existing store and deciding what keywords, pages and backlinks you already have before optimizing.
steps: Enter your domain into a domain-analysis tool; the source notes it crawls for around ten minutes and then reports existing keywords, which keywords are currently ranking, and organic traffic directed based on monthly estimates.
Review the backlink data it returns to learn where links to your site were created, and use the trending chart to understand your organic traffic graph over time.
Use a separate paid tool (the source names HRF) when you want to see traffic and keyword flow rather than domain-level rankings.
Use the output to prioritize: pages ranking on page two or three are usually closer to gains than pages with no impressions at all.
Re-run the audit after catalog or content changes, because monthly estimates and rankings shift.
Verify current tool interfaces and pricing before committing, since third-party SEO tools change frequently.
caveats: The source's tool examples are illustrative; traffic figures from third-party tools are estimates, not analytics-grade data.
The ten-minute crawl estimate is the presenter's observation of one tool, not a standard.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Build link authority through third-party backlinks and guest posts
cards.summary: Earn inbound links on relevant external sites using keyword anchor text, and treat links as harder to win from high-authority domains.
cards.use_when: Off-page SEO planning when you need to build domain trust and referral traffic to product or category pages.
steps: Map your target keyword (e.g. 'switch power cord') and search your backlink profile for links using that anchor text; the source finds many keywords with zero links, showing the gap.
Pursue guest posts and contributed content: the source shows a third-party article titled around a product/brand keyword whose anchor text links back to the store.
Confirm the anchor text and target URL in each earned link, since this is how the source defines a backlink reaching your site.

Target relevant, high-authority hosts, but expect rejection: the source says listing on news, media, education and government domains is hard and typically follows reputation, domain score and marketing success.
Expect link loss over time — the source notes admins delete links, so audit your profile periodically rather than assuming permanence.
Recognize inbound vs. outbound: a link into you is inbound; a link from you to another site is outbound — both pass context but only inbound builds your authority.
caveats: The source's own backlink example includes a link that had been removed, illustrating volatility.
Do not equate a link on a trusted domain with a guaranteed ranking lift — the source frames it as helpful for getting authorized, not a certainty.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Run local SEO with NAP-consistent business listings and near-me keywords
cards.summary: Claim and maintain a Google Business Profile with exact name, address and phone, then target location-modified keywords for map-pack visibility.
cards.use_when: Local or multi-location stores wanting visibility in map results and 'near me' searches.
steps: Set up and verify a Google Business Profile — the source calls Google the best and most important listing; it is typically verified by postcard, business phone or business email.

Maintain NAP consistency (name, address, phone) across every citation the source lists; it says a listing without these three will not qualify or be approved, while images, products and directions are optional additions.
Target local keyword patterns for content and titles: 'near me', 'best [product] near me', '[product] in [city]' and '[product] in [state]'.
Build citations across directories that match your real business data, since the source describes citations as internet references carrying employee/company name, phone and address.
Monitor reviews on the profile, as the source treats review content as part of the listing's value.
Re-audit NAP after moves, rebrands or phone changes, since inconsistency undermines verification.
caveats: The source's local-SEO discussion is conceptual and does not benchmark traffic or revenue outcomes.
Verification methods change over time — check Google's current verification process before following the source's method.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use YouTube SEO to drive store discovery and traffic
cards.summary: Create audience-specific videos with keyworded titles, descriptions and thumbnails, and link back to the store to grow visibility and traffic.
cards.use_when: Adding video to the acquisition mix for product education, unboxing, or how-to content that should feed the store.
steps: Create videos aimed at a specific audience rather than broad topics, since the source frames YouTube as a way to increase visibility and website traffic.
Draft catchy, clickable titles and write descriptions containing relevant keywords and phrases; add tags, hashtags and the correct category.
Upload a personalized thumbnail — the source calls it the first impression — and notes you can modify an uploaded image with AI tools.
Include relevant links back to your store in the video and channel description so viewers can convert.
Track performance in YouTube Analytics (views per video, top content, traffic over time) to see which topics move and double down.
Remember YouTube is free to produce on and has no content ceiling, which the source frames as a low-cost traffic channel.
caveats: The source describes channel analytics examples with small view counts; treat any view or traffic result as an example, not a benchmark.
Video SEO does not replace site SEO — the source presents it as an additional acquisition channel.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Write engaging content that keeps shoppers on the page and clicking
cards.summary: Produce valuable, relevant content so visitors stay, engage and act — reducing bounce and increasing clicks on add-to-cart and contact actions.
cards.use_when: Improving PDP copy, category descriptions or blog content that currently gets traffic but no engagement.
steps: Lead with value and relevance: the source repeats that content is king and that people comment, like and stay when information is genuinely useful.
Design the content to prompt specific actions — the source names add to cart, contact-us form and link clicks as engagement outcomes.
Monitor page views, time on page and bounce rate; the source states a higher bounce rate is generally bad, and engaging content is the countermeasure.
Support long-form content with proper H2/H3 structure so it's readable and scannable, tying back to the heading-tag rules.
Interlink from content to relevant product and category pages so engagement translates into product discovery.
Note the trade-offs the source lists for blogging as an off-page activity: it benefits SEO and maintains client contact but is time-consuming and requires a constant stream of fresh ideas.
caveats: The source asserts high bounce rate is generally bad without giving a numeric threshold — interpret against your own baseline by page type.
Engagement metrics alone don't prove revenue impact; pair with conversion measurement.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Audit technical SEO health: HTTPS, responsiveness, load time, sitemap, schema, citations
cards.summary: Run through the source's technical-SEO checklist — security, responsiveness, speed, sitemap, schema, citations and error fixes — to keep a store crawlable and rankable.
cards.use_when: Periodic technical SEO audit of a store, or as a pre-launch checklist for a new site or replatform.
steps: Verify HTTPS: open the site and confirm the padlock/secure connection; the source says you need an HTTPS URL, not HTTP, which would show as insecure.
Check responsiveness across mobile, tablet and desktop, confirming layout and load behavior hold up on each.
Measure load time and target the source's under-one-to-two-second guideline, trimming heavy media as needed.
Confirm the XML sitemap exists and is submitted so pages can be crawled and indexed.
Validate schema/structured-data markup for the page types you rely on (product, reviews, local business).
Check local citation NAP consistency if you have physical locations, since the source says incomplete NAP blocks listing approval.
Fix blocking errors: 404/not-found pages, slow pages, and 403-type errors, redirecting dead URLs to relevant pages.
Add newly shipped site features and product changes to the technical plan, because the source argues nothing in marketing stays static.
caveats: These are the source's priority factors, not an exhaustive or official ranking-factor list.
Search algorithms change frequently per the source, so re-audit rather than treating one pass as permanent.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Keep technical SEO current as search algorithms change
cards.summary: Treat algorithm updates as recurring filters that remove irrelevant results, and keep updating site structure, features and content to stay compliant.
cards.use_when: Planning an SEO roadmap or deciding how much to invest in technical maintenance versus one-off optimizations.
steps: Assume algorithms will keep changing: the source says Google continually revises how it filters its database and removes irrelevant content.
Budget for regular technical updates rather than a one-time fix, aligning site architecture and content with current guidelines.
When adding site or product features (new product lines, case studies, customer-support content), update the technical SEO layer accordingly so new pages are crawlable and correctly marked up.
Watch for penalty risk: the source says sites not following Google's guidelines can be penalized and fail to rank — the reason it stresses guideline compliance.
Recheck assumptions periodically, since the source notes SEO that was easy 8-10 years ago is harder precisely because everyone does the same things.
Verify current algorithm guidance from Google rather than relying on any course material, including this one, for the latest specifics.
caveats: The source presents algorithms as a general mechanism for filtering relevance and warns about penalties; it does not claim a specific update caused a specific ranking change.
Algorithm guidance dates quickly — always confirm the current state of the algorithm and guidelines.
